entries.description: Cloudflare network outage on 2025-11-18. Cloudflare's own post-mortem states it was not caused by a cyber attack; its team had briefly suspected an attack because its off-network status page also failed.
entries.why_not_a_major_incident: As an attack/breach event it is a false alarm: root cause was an internal Bot Management feature-file generation fault after a database permissions change. Caveat: the outage itself was large and real, so it is a negative only for 'cyberattack/breach' classification.

entries.description: Iberian blackout of 2025-04-28 triggered early speculation of a cyberattack. Spain's grid operator and later the energy minister reported no sign of one.
entries.why_not_a_major_incident: Cyberattack hypothesis not supported: authorities reported no intrusion in control systems and no sign of attack on generation control centres. Caveat: the blackout itself was a major real outage.

entries.verification_notes: Headlines are og:title values. The Politico page's own <title> adds ' – POLITICO'. Reuters description: Energy Minister Sara Aagesen said Spain found no indication of a cyberattack on power generation control centres. Event date 2025-04-28 is stated in the Reuters description.

entries.description: FAA NOTAM system outage on 2023-01-11 prompted cyberattack questions. FAA preliminary review traced it to contract personnel unintentionally deleting files while correcting database synchronisation.
entries.why_not_a_major_incident: FAA stated it found no evidence of a cyber attack or malicious intent. Caveat: operational impact (flight delays) was real; the negative is for the cyberattack interpretation.

entries.description: Facebook, Instagram and WhatsApp global outage on 2021-10-04. Meta attributed it to configuration changes on backbone routers, not malicious activity.
entries.why_not_a_major_incident: Not a hack or breach: Meta said it was an error of its own making and that it had no evidence user data was compromised. Caveat: the outage was large and real.

entries.description: Global Windows outage of 2024-07-19 hit Australian banks, airports, supermarkets and telcos. Australian officials said there was no evidence of a cyber-security incident.
entries.why_not_a_major_incident: Cyber-incident interpretation was a false alarm: attributed to a technical issue from a CrowdStrike update. Caveat: the outage was very large; negative only for 'cyberattack/breach' classification.

entries.verification_notes: ABC live blog quotes Home Affairs Minister Clare O'Neil: no evidence the outages were caused by a cyber-security incident, result of a 'technical issue caused by a Crowdstrike update'. SMH quote scraped: 'There is no information to suggest it is a cybersecurity incident.' Headlines are page <title> values (ABC og:title is "'Completely unprecedented' outage causes havoc with IT systems across globe — as it happened"; SMH og:title is "'Largest IT outage in history' caused by US-based cybersecurity firm", which is the later headline for the same URL).

entries.description: Media reported a Telstra data breach after about 30,000 employee names and email addresses were posted online. Telstra stated no Telstra system was breached and the data was from 2017 held by a third party.
entries.why_not_a_major_incident: Headline framing implies a Telstra breach; Telstra said there was no breach of any Telstra systems, no customer account information was involved and the data dated from 2017.

sources.headline_verbatim: Telstra, NAB staff info stolen in third-party data breach
Employee data breach: what you need to know

entries.verification_notes: SMH headline is the og:title; the page's <title> tag reads 'Tesltra breach: 30,000 current, former workers’ emails stolen' (sic, typo as scraped), likely the earlier headline - the more alarming framing. Telstra page states 'There has been no breach of Telstra’s systems' and that the data was from 2017. Telstra page date '04 October 2022' read from page text. Weakness: the underlying third-party breach was real, so this is misleading by attribution rather than fabricated.

entries.description: Pro-Russian group Killnet DDoS attacks took some US airport websites offline on 2022-10-10. Headlines referred to 'cyberattacks on airports'; reports state flights and airport operations were not affected.
entries.why_not_a_major_incident: Impact limited to temporary public website unavailability; no operational, safety or data impact reported.

entries.verification_notes: NPR headline is the page <title> (minus ' : NPR'); its h1/og:title reads 'Pro-Russian hackers claim responsibility for knocking U.S. airport websites offline' and og:description says officials said the outages did not interrupt operations. Dark Reading search snippet said sites inaccessible for several hours with no apparent operational impact (snippet only).
